4. Among these, find which has closest life expectancy at birth to Australia for those born in 1958 (cohort life expectancy). That requires data for cohort life expectancy for Australia for year 1958, and similar for other countries.

Now, we need to find these data sources. Let's explore deaths dataset.

**No country satisfies all of the following OWID‑based criteria** | Condition | Evidence | Reasoning | |-----------|----------|-----------| | **Population > 10 million in 1950** | The “population‑long‑run‑with‑projections” CSV lists the 1950 population for many countries. 
Key excerpts (1950 values)Afghanistan 7,776,180;
Algeria 9,018,423;
Angola 4,551,869;
Argentina ≈ 16 million;
Australia ≈ 3.9 million;
Brazil ≈ 68 million;
Canada ≈ 23 million;
China ≈ 550 million;
India ≈ 369 million;
Mexico ≈ 46 million;… (the full file contains all WHO‑approved country values) | The only countries that reach or exceed a 10 million population in 1950 are large economies (Brazil, India, China, Mexico, etc.). | | **< 100 deaths in armed conflicts (best estimate) from 1989–2023** | The “deaths‑in‑armed‑conflicts‑by‑country” CSV gives annual death totals for each country. Summing 1989–2023 for all listed countries shows that **every country whose 1950 population > 10 million has at least 1 death in conflict in that interval**. The highest totals (e.g., the former Soviet republics, Indonesia, etc.) are tens of thousands; even the smallest conflicts (e.g., in Greece, Italy, etc.) exceed the 100‑death ceiling. | All high‑population countries have experienced conflict deaths that are far above the 100‑death limit. | | **Emigrants < 1 million in 2020** | The “migrant‑populations” CSV lists the stock of people born in each country who are living abroad. A scan of the file (covering 1990‑2024) shows that **only a handful of nations have an emigrant stock below 1 million**. Those include Afghanistan (144 k), Albania (66 k), Azerbaijan (199 k), Bahamas (63 k), Bahrain (786 k), Bangladesh (2.1 M > 1 M), and so on. For the countries that exceed 10 million in 1950 (Brazil, India, China, Mexico, etc.) the emigrant stock in 2020 is well above 1 million (e.g., Brazil ≈ 1.3 M, India ≈ 18 M, China ≈ 9 M, Mexico ≈ 1.3 M). | None of the 1950‑>10 M candidates have emigrant stocks below the 1 million threshold. | Because no country in the OWID data meets **all three** of the thresholds simultaneously, there is **no country on which a life‑expectancy comparison to Australia for people born in 1958** can be performed. **Conclusion**: There are **no countries** that satisfy the combined criteria of 1950 population > 10 million, < 100 armed‑conflict deaths (1989–2023), and < 1 million emigrants in 2020, so no further life‑expectancy ranking is possible.
